source.title: I found >800 orthogonal "write code" steering vectors

page_placements.theme: Steering depends on coefficient, context, composition and geometry

record.file_problem: none; full post and comments are present
record.tranche_reason: The post discusses superposition as a possible explanation, but its experiments optimize and apply steering vectors; they do not test the toy-model feature-storage claim or the listed claims about represented features, neurons, or SAE units.
record.gate_note: The reported results concern optimized orthogonal steering vectors and their effects on outputs. They do not establish that these vectors are the model's represented features. The post's hypotheses about superposition and feature redundancy are not experimental tests of those claims. The listed links to output files and plots are not treated as additional inspected results.
record.test_reason: The post optimizes steering vectors orthogonal to a MELBO vector so that they reproduce the same layer-16 activations, then reports their count, norms and output effects. Nothing here measures features stored in superposition, neuron polysemanticity, SAE features or feature dimensionality. Superposition appears only as one of several hypotheses, and the author calls it post-hoc and untested. The vectors are found by optimization and are not shown to be features the model represents.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The author finds hundreds of orthogonal steering vectors with similar effects and remains confused about why. Redundant representation due to superposition and adversarial or out-of-distribution vectors are offered only as hypotheses, and neither is tested.
record.recipe_differences: The experiments use MELBO-derived steering vectors and a new optimization procedure that finds orthogonal vectors matching layer-16 activations; they do not reproduce the original toy-model method.
record.method_sensitivity: The outcomes vary with vector type and generation index. Coding vectors work well through much of the early sequence but degrade later; KL plots are reported as less informative for the alien and STEM cases. Averaging results also depend on scaling, and unscaled averages depend on the number of vectors averaged.

fits_no_version.finding: About 1558 orthogonal vectors were generated for the coding vector. Those up to the 800s steer outputs toward code, but only at norm ~20 versus the base vector's norm of 7. Rescaled to norm 7, they produce refusals.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A single behavior can be induced by many mutually orthogonal activation-steering vectors, and these need not correspond to distinct represented features.

fits_no_version.finding: Unscaled averages of the coding vectors fail to produce code. Averages scaled by √n do produce code, while scaled averages are inconsistent for the alien, STEM and jailbreak vectors.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Whether orthogonal steering interventions compose depends on their scale and on the behavior being steered.

fits_no_version.finding: The author estimates about 800 meaningful alien and STEM vectors each. KL plots do not mark where these vectors stop being meaningful.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The apparent number of useful orthogonal steering vectors, and how well a given metric detects them, depend on the target behavior.

record.problems: The author describes the investigation as preliminary and says the mechanism is unclear. Most behavioral evidence is qualitative and focused on one model and a bomb prompt; no error estimates or controlled random-vector comparison is reported in the post. The author notes that KL divergence at the last token may be a small sample and can be misleading for some target behaviors.
record.rows_left_out: No reported result rows were left out. The post links to additional output files and plots, which are not included as inspected results.

untested.parts: No toy model, sparsity sweep or feature geometry.
No neuron-level polysemanticity or capacity allocation measured.
No feature-to-neuron spread or SAE recovery measured. The orthogonal steering vectors are not shown to be the model's features.
The existence of many orthogonal vectors that produce coding is not analysed as a test of 1-D versus multi-dimensional features.

record.verdict_notes: All rows are correctly linked to none. Commenters offer high-dimensional geometry explanations (Fabien Roger, Kaarel's cap bound) and a nonlinear-map explanation (Atmyre's layer-16 cosine plots); these are comments, not the author's results, and were reasonably left out as rows. Atmyre's comparison against random vectors is the only control-like evidence, and it appears only in a comment.

versions.untested_parts: No toy network, sparse-feature count, feature-storage geometry, sparsity transition, or regular geometry is tested.
No neuron polysemanticity, capacity allocation, or importance-dependent feature sharing is measured.
No polysemantic neurons or alternative causes of neuron polysemanticity are measured.
No feature-to-neuron distribution or SAE-recovered feature is measured.
No SAE features or their completeness, stability, or canonical status are studied.
The study finds steering vectors, but does not test whether represented or superposed features are one-dimensional rather than multidimensional.

relation.reason: Superposition motivates a speculative redundancy explanation. The author presents alternative explanations and leaves them unresolved.

tranche.reason: The experiments measure optimized steering vectors and their behavioral effects; they neither test a catalog claim version nor use superposition as an established methodological tool.

source_check.notes: The reported outcomes are faithful qualitative steering observations. The scaled-mean results come from an author comment and provide no n-specific success rates; they do not establish superposition.

statements.correction: Unscaled first-20 average: refusal; first-3 average: jailbreak; first-2 average: code, refusal, or mixture depending on the run. Coding-vector mean multiplied by √n: reported to produce coding behavior. Scaled alien means: similar style, fewer bomb mentions. Scaled STEM means: STEM problems or jailbreaks. Scaled jailbreak means: jailbreaks or first- or second-person stories.
statements.problem: The unqualified claim that unscaled coding-vector averages fail omits that averaging the first two sometimes produces code. Alien-vector means retain a similar style, so their composition is not simply a failure.
